newsitem.title: USA: James Unruh resigns as Unisys chairman, CEO.
newsitem.headline: James Unruh resigns as Unisys chairman, CEO.

text.p: James Unruh has resigned as chairman and chief executive officer of Unisys Corp. after seven years at the helm of the struggling computer maker.
Unisys announced on Thursday that Unruh, 56, will step down as chief executive officer once a successor is named, and will remain chairman until the company's next annual meeting in April 1998.

Unruh has overseen four restructurings of Unisys. Under his leadership, the company has laid off tens of thousands of employees, closed plants, pared product lines and sold divisions, but has not been able to consistently report revenue growth.

Unisys was formed by the 1986 merger of Sperry Corp. and Burroughs Corp. It enjoyed a few years of growth, fueled mainly by cost-cutting, but then entered a prolonged slump as mainframe computers, its chief product, lost favor amid the rise of smaller, cheaper machines.
Unisys reported a 1997 first quarter loss of $0.06 per share, and a loss for all of 1996 of $0.41 per share.
